concepts.label: node
concepts.statement: A node carries local properties but has no obligation to declare what it is, how it is used, or what it means.
concepts.section: Nodes Have No Obligation to Explain Themselves
concepts.quote: A node in a graph is just a node. It may carry some local properties — a title, a value, a timestamp — but it has no inherent obligation to declare what it "is," how it should be used, or what it means.

concepts.label: meaning through connectivity
concepts.statement: What a thing is emerges from the edges traceable from it.
concepts.section: Nodes Have No Obligation to Explain Themselves
concepts.quote: In a graph-first model, what something "is" emerges from the edges you can trace from it.

concepts.label: connectivity
concepts.statement: A node is meaningful in proportion to how richly it is connected.
concepts.section: Nodes Have No Obligation to Explain Themselves
concepts.quote: A node connected to a rich web of other nodes is meaningful in proportion to that connectivity.

concepts.label: schema-first
concepts.statement: The type system tells you what something is before you encounter it.
concepts.section: Nodes Have No Obligation to Explain Themselves
concepts.quote: schema-first thinking, where the type system tells you what something is before you encounter it

concepts.label: declared meaning
concepts.statement: Meaning asserted by a schema, which instances conform to or fail.
concepts.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
concepts.quote: In a schema-first system, meaning is declared: "This object IS a Task. It HAS these fields. Its status MUST be one of these values." The schema is the authority, and instances conform or fail validation.

concepts.label: discovered meaning
concepts.statement: Meaning determined by traversing a node's edges.
concepts.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
concepts.quote: In a graph-first system, meaning is discovered: "This node has edges to other nodes. By traversing those edges, we can determine what this node relates to, what constraints apply, and how confidently we can characterise it."

concepts.label: compatibility
concepts.statement: The degree to which two nodes' subgraphs overlap when traced toward common reference points.
concepts.quote: Two nodes are not compatible because they share a type declaration. They are compatible to the degree that their subgraphs overlap when traced toward common reference points.

concepts.label: the fractal principle
concepts.statement: The same structural pattern, nodes with edges and meaning through connectivity, repeats at every level of zoom.
concepts.section: Every Scope Defines Its Own Vocabulary
concepts.quote: the same structural pattern — nodes with edges, meaning through connectivity — repeats at every level of zoom

concepts.label: local vocabulary
concepts.statement: Every level of the scope hierarchy can introduce its own nodes, edges, types and definitions.
concepts.section: Every Scope Defines Its Own Vocabulary
concepts.quote: Every level in this hierarchy can introduce its own nodes, edges, types, and definitions.

concepts.label: name clash
concepts.statement: Label collisions between scopes, expected and resolved structurally rather than by name.
concepts.quote: In a fractal system, name clashes are inevitable and non-problematic.

concepts.label: the Semantic Web
concepts.statement: The community that identified the right problem: exchanging meaning without agreeing on everything upfront.
concepts.quote: The Semantic Web community identified the right problem: how do independent parties exchange meaning without agreeing on everything upfront?

concepts.label: anchor node
concepts.statement: A node that is well-connected, well-maintained and well-known, with no special authority.
concepts.quote: An anchor node is simply a node that:

concepts.label: the confidence spectrum
concepts.statement: Every assertion about a node sits on a spectrum from no edges to rich multi-hop connectivity.
concepts.quote: Every assertion the system makes about a node sits on a confidence spectrum:

concepts.label: honest uncertainty
concepts.statement: The default posture: report what the edges support, what is missing, and what that does to confidence.
concepts.quote: The system's default posture is honest uncertainty

concepts.label: enrichment
concepts.statement: The response to low confidence: add edges rather than fail validation.
concepts.quote: the response is not validation failure. It is an opportunity for enrichment

concepts.label: graphs of graphs
concepts.statement: The ecosystem is not one flat graph; it is a graph of graphs, recursively.
concepts.quote: It is a graph of graphs, recursively

concepts.label: cross-graph edge
concepts.statement: An edge that crosses from one sovereign graph into another, carrying meaning between them.
concepts.quote: it creates an edge that crosses from the Issues-FS graph into the osbot-utils Type_Safe graph

concepts.label: version pinning
concepts.statement: A cross-graph edge may pin meaning to a version or float with the latest; the graph records the choice.
concepts.quote: If the edge points to `osbot-utils@3.63.4`, then the meaning is pinned to that version's definition.

concepts.label: the Lexicon
concepts.statement: Not a dictionary or a schema registry: curated anchor nodes, cross-graph edges, traversal tools and overridable bootstrap definitions.
concepts.quote: the Issues-FS Lexicon is not a dictionary or a schema registry

concepts.label: the Librarian
concepts.statement: Used twice as the agent who adds or arbitrates edges; never defined in this document.
concepts.quote: A human or a Librarian agent can then decide

concepts.label: Type_Safe
concepts.statement: The runtime type framework the port example leans on; assumed, not defined here.
concepts.quote: Consider a concrete example from the osbot-utils Type_Safe framework:

concepts.label: ROLE.md
concepts.statement: Used as the thing that makes a role meaningful; its own format is never defined here.
concepts.quote: If it links to a ROLE.md definition, to a set of issue types it can create, to handoff protocols — then we know what this QA role does.

concepts.label: the central claim
concepts.statement: Everything is a graph; meaning is discovered through relationships, not declared; confidence is proportional to connectivity.
concepts.quote: everything is a graph, meaning is not declared but discovered through graph relationships, and confidence in that meaning is proportional to how richly connected a node is to other nodes that provide context

concepts.label: not a metaphor
concepts.statement: The claim is a literal architectural principle, not a metaphor.
concepts.quote: This is not a metaphor. It is a literal architectural principle

concepts.label: no edges, no meaning
concepts.statement: A node connected to nothing is, literally, meaningless.
concepts.section: Nodes Have No Obligation to Explain Themselves
concepts.quote: A node connected to nothing is meaningless — literally.

concepts.label: the difference is connectivity
concepts.statement: Two identical values differ radically in meaning when their connectivity differs.
concepts.quote: **The difference is not in the value.** Both scenarios have `8080`. The difference is in the **connectivity**.

concepts.label: the graph provides the evidence or it does not
concepts.statement: The system reports what it can and cannot confirm rather than assuming meaning.
concepts.quote: The graph either provides the evidence or it doesn't. The system's job is to report what it can and can't confirm, not to assume meaning where the edges don't support it.

concepts.label: declared is brittle, discovered is resilient
concepts.statement: Declared meaning breaks at boundaries; discovered meaning thins but composes.
concepts.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
concepts.quote: declared meaning is brittle and local

concepts.label: common ground is discovered, not imposed
concepts.statement: Structural overlap can be found across five different review processes without any team conforming to a shared schema.
concepts.section: Finding Common Ground Through Graph Analysis
concepts.quote: The common ground was *discovered* in the graph, not *imposed* on it.

concepts.label: compatibility is a spectrum
concepts.statement: Compatibility is not binary, not symmetric, not global, and it is computable.
concepts.quote: **Not binary** — it's a spectrum (Team A and Team C are more compatible than Team A and Team B)

concepts.label: no registration with the parent
concepts.statement: A child scope never needs to register its vocabulary with a parent scope.
concepts.section: Every Scope Defines Its Own Vocabulary
concepts.quote: At no level does a child scope need to "register" its vocabulary with a parent scope.

concepts.label: resolution is structural
concepts.statement: Name clashes resolve by graph identity and traversal path, not by the label.
concepts.quote: Resolution is structural, not nominal.

concepts.label: observations, not errors
concepts.statement: Gaps, partial mappings and contradictions are surfaced for judgement, not rejected as failures.
concepts.section: Incompatibility and Missing Pieces Are Expected
concepts.quote: None of these are errors. They are observations that the graph analysis can make, surfacing them for human (or agent) judgment.

concepts.label: the Semantic Web's mistake
concepts.statement: The mistake was attaching meaning to nodes rather than deriving it from edges.
concepts.quote: They ended up attaching meaning *to nodes* rather than deriving meaning *from edges*.

concepts.label: schema-first in graph syntax
concepts.statement: Self-describing nodes are schema-first thinking wearing graph syntax.
concepts.quote: This is schema-first thinking dressed in graph syntax. The node knows what it is.

concepts.label: mappings can come from anyone
concepts.statement: Cross-reference edges may be added by the team, an agent, an analysis or a third party, without touching the original node.
concepts.quote: the mappings might have been added by anyone: the team itself, a Librarian agent, an automated analysis, or a third party doing an integration

concepts.label: anchors have no special authority
concepts.statement: An anchor node enables discovery; it does not force conformity.
concepts.quote: **Has no special authority** — it does not force conformity; it enables discovery

concepts.label: confidence is computable
concepts.statement: How confident the system is about a node is always computable from the graph.
concepts.quote: the answer is always computable from the graph: count the edges, measure the depth of traversal to anchor nodes, assess the authority of the nodes reached

concepts.label: gaps are never filled with assumptions
concepts.statement: The system reports found and missing edges and never fills gaps by assuming.
concepts.quote: It never fills in the gaps with assumptions.

concepts.label: grow the graph, do not tighten the schema
concepts.statement: The ecosystem improves by adding edges, not by imposing stricter schemas.
concepts.quote: not by imposing stricter schemas, but by growing the graph

concepts.label: each graph is sovereign
concepts.statement: Cross-graph edges give interoperability across teams, languages, cultures and agendas without any graph changing internally.
concepts.quote: This is what makes the graph model scale across teams, languages, cultures, and agendas. Each graph is sovereign.

concepts.label: pin or float, but say which
concepts.statement: Pinned and floating version edges are both valid; the graph makes the choice explicit and traceable.
concepts.quote: Both are valid choices. The graph makes the choice explicit and traceable.

concepts.label: local override is a capability
concepts.statement: Any scope may override or specialise bootstrap definitions by creating local nodes with different subgraphs.
concepts.quote: **Override or specialise** bootstrap definitions by creating local nodes with different subgraphs

concepts.label: we know, we think, we cannot confirm
concepts.statement: The system's observations end in a three-state honest assessment.
concepts.quote: **Generate honest assessments**: "We know X. We think Y. We cannot confirm Z."

concepts.label: authority is not identity
concepts.statement: Authority is a property of connectivity, provenance and governance, not of identity.
concepts.quote: authority is a property of connectivity, provenance, and governance, not of identity

concepts.label: connection is structural, not nominal
concepts.statement: A Japanese-labelled process connects to an English-labelled anchor through edges, with no shared label needed.
concepts.quote: The connection is structural (via graph edges), not nominal (via shared label).

concepts.label: the review chain is traceable
concepts.statement: A three-city review chain in three languages is traceable end to end through the graph.
concepts.quote: The review chain is traceable through the graph.

concepts.label: absence is reported, not papered over
concepts.statement: The system does not pretend a GitHub issue is a Feature_Request; it reports the missing edge and what adding it would enable.
concepts.section: The Open Source Contributor in Nairobi
concepts.quote: The system doesn't pretend the GitHub issue is a Feature_Request just because a human would make that inference.

concepts.label: the document compresses itself to ten principles
concepts.statement: The summary lists ten core principles. The first edition distilled five ideas from this source; the gap is ladder finding 3.
concepts.quote: 1. **Everything is a node.** Nodes carry local properties but have no obligation to declare what they are or how they should be used.

concepts.label: distributed vocabulary produces gaps
concepts.statement: A fractal system with distributed vocabulary will inevitably produce gaps, partial mappings and contradictions.
concepts.section: Incompatibility and Missing Pieces Are Expected
concepts.quote: A fractal system with distributed vocabulary will inevitably produce:

concepts.label: meaning thins measurably at boundaries
concepts.statement: Crossing a boundary thins meaning rather than breaking it, and the system can report exactly how thin.
concepts.section: Meaning Is Not Declared — It Is Discovered
concepts.quote: it just means some edges don't extend across that boundary, and the meaning becomes thinner (less confident) on the other side

concepts.label: every edge grows self-understanding
concepts.statement: Each added edge increments the system's understanding of itself; the ecosystem improves this way over time.
concepts.quote: Every edge added is a small increment in the system's understanding of itself.

concepts.label: be the foundation
concepts.statement: Underpin every other document in the ecosystem: the philosophy everything else is built on.
concepts.quote: This is the foundational document for the Issues-FS ecosystem.

concepts.statement: Two scenarios with the identical value 8080, differing only in connectivity, yield radically different meaning.
concepts.quote: class Safe_UInt__Port(Safe_UInt):

concepts.statement: Five teams' Review processes, none aware of the others, analysed for structural overlap without any conforming.
concepts.quote: Consider five different teams, each with a process they call "Review":

concepts.statement: A SKOS prefLabel declaration shown as meaning encoded on the node itself: the mistake, in six lines.

concepts.statement: London, Tokyo, Frankfurt and Nairobi: one task, three review vocabularies, one unmapped proposal, every confidence statement computed.

terms.label: structure
terms.def: An arrangement of parts that carries information in how the parts relate.

terms.label: graph
terms.def: A structure of nodes and edges; here always a network graph, never a chart.

terms.label: node
terms.def: A point in a graph; carries local properties but no obligation to explain itself.

terms.label: edge
terms.def: A connection between two nodes; where meaning actually lives.

terms.label: ontology
terms.def: The account of what kinds of things exist and how the kinds relate.

terms.label: taxonomy
terms.def: A classification by kind-of relations; the tree inside the ontology.

terms.label: semantics
terms.def: What expressions mean, as opposed to how they are written.

terms.label: meaning
terms.def: What a thing is, discovered through the edges traceable from it.

terms.label: connectivity
terms.def: How richly a node is joined to nodes that provide context; confidence grows with it.

terms.label: identifier
terms.def: A name that picks out one thing; only useful when stable.

terms.label: hash
terms.def: A content-derived identifier: the same content always yields the same hash.

terms.label: token
terms.def: A unit of text with an identity; in the WCLM the identity is its hash.

terms.label: word
terms.def: The smallest carrier of meaning in a document; here every word is a token with no vocabulary cap.

terms.label: document
terms.def: A frozen body of text; the ground truth every graph here is anchored to.

terms.label: anchor
terms.def: A verified pointer from a claim to the exact bytes that support it.

terms.label: provenance
terms.def: Where something came from and the path it took; the etymology of a claim.

terms.label: weight
terms.def: A stated numeric formula over graph inputs; here always readable, never fitted.

terms.label: layer
terms.def: One named transformation in the engine, with declared inputs and outputs.

terms.label: transformer
terms.def: A stack of layers that turns a prompt into an answer; here every layer is deterministic.

terms.label: attention
terms.def: Which tokens look at which, and how hard; here co-occurrence and binding made visible.

terms.label: abstraction
terms.def: A level above the detail where the real connections appear.

terms.label: primitive
terms.def: A building block other things are defined in terms of.

terms.label: principle
terms.def: A rule that survives across cases; heavier than any single example.

terms.label: task
terms.def: A unit of work with a done-state; the atom of a workflow.

terms.label: workflow
terms.def: Tasks joined by order and condition; development runs on these.

terms.label: development
terms.def: The whole practice of building software: designing, writing, testing, shipping.

terms.label: qa
terms.def: Quality assurance: the checking half of building; not a random word.

terms.label: testing
terms.def: Executable doubt: running the work to see whether it holds.

terms.label: versioning
terms.def: Keeping every state of a thing addressable, so change becomes data.

terms.label: version file system
terms.def: A filesystem where history is first-class; the ground issues-fs stands on.

terms.label: filesystem
terms.def: Named content in named places; the oldest graph most people use.

terms.label: issues-fs
terms.def: The ecosystem the pilot document founds: issues as files, meaning through connectivity.

terms.label: claim
terms.def: A statement a document makes, anchored to its bytes; judged elsewhere.

terms.label: concept
terms.def: A named idea a document uses; defined by its connections, not its label.

terms.label: example
terms.def: A concrete case that demonstrates a claim; where abstractions touch ground.

graph.label: the network graph
graph.def: Nodes joined by edges; meaning through connectivity. The sense reached through this document's own connections: graph connects to network, to nodes and edges, to mathematics, to the fractal principle.

graph.label: a chart of data
graph.def: Bars, lines and axes drawn from numbers: 'the sales graph is up'. No nodes, no edges — a picture of quantities, not of connections.

graph.label: the graph of a function
graph.def: The curve of y = f(x) drawn on axes. A set of points satisfying an equation — connectivity plays no part.

graph.label: graph paper
graph.def: The printed square grid you draw on. The word names the ruled page itself, not anything drawn upon it.

graph.label: the social graph
graph.def: Who follows whom, who is friends with whom. The closest industry sense to this document's: it IS a network graph, wearing a product name.

node.label: a point in a graph
node.def: A thing that exists by being connected: a node holds edges, and what it means emerges from what those edges reach.

node.label: Node.js, the runtime
node.def: The JavaScript runtime ('does it run on Node?'). A product name, no relation to graph structure.

node.label: a lymph node
node.def: A small gland of the immune system. In a clinic, 'swollen nodes' has nothing to do with edges.

node.label: a stem node
node.def: The joint on a plant stem where a leaf or branch grows. Gardeners cut just above one.

node.label: a machine on the network
node.def: Any device with an address: a server, a switch, a sensor. Nearer to this document's sense — the machines really are vertices of a network — but the word names hardware, not structure.

fractal.label: the fractal principle
fractal.def: The same structural pattern — nodes with edges, meaning through connectivity — repeating at every level of zoom: a graph of graphs, every scope defining its own vocabulary.

fractal.label: a self-similar set
fractal.def: Mandelbrot and Koch: a set whose parts resemble the whole at every magnification, with fractional dimension.

fractal.label: fractal art
fractal.def: Images rendered from iterating those sets: posters, album covers, screen savers.

fractal.label: a fractal antenna
fractal.def: A self-similar conductor shape that packs a long electrical length into a small space; in phones and RFID tags.

fractal.label: endlessly nested (figurative)
fractal.def: 'The problem is fractal': every part turns out to have parts. Borrowed imagery, no geometry claimed.

task.label: a node someone called Task
task.def: The document's own example: an issue labelled 'Task' is just a node — only its edges to a definition say what a Task is, and that definition changes with culture and context.

task.label: a unit of work
task.def: Something with an owner, an estimate and a due date, living on a board between 'to do' and 'done'.

task.label: a running process
task.def: A scheduled unit of execution: the task manager, a task switch, kill the task.

task.label: a household chore
task.def: Something on the list for the weekend. No board, no scheduler — just the oldest sense of the word.

maps.why: finance nests workbooks inside workbooks inside consolidation packs — the same structure at every zoom, and everyone in the room has lived it
a named cell means nothing alone; its formula references — what it reads, what reads it — are what make it matter
a number in the group accounts IS its roll-up: subsidiary lines, eliminations, adjustments — remove the trail and the number is just ink
the shared reference everyone maps their local codes to, so two subsidiaries can disagree locally and still consolidate
every working paper can open into schedules with their own working papers — the same review structure repeats at every level
an explicit, checkable link between two entities' books — the connection is real only when both sides carry it
an incident runbook steps into service runbooks that step into host procedures — nested procedures with the same shape at every level

maps.say: a host behind a service name
maps.why: the box matters only through what routes to it and what it depends on; an unplugged host with no traffic is inventory, not infrastructure
what a service IS operationally is what it calls and what calls it — the map, not the name, tells you the blast radius
the agreed reference record every team points at, so local naming can vary without losing the thread
operations never pretends binary certainty: a page, a warning and an info line are graded confidence, and the grade is part of the signal
a body is systems of organs of tissues of cells — clinicians reason at every level and switch zoom mid-sentence
a symptom means almost nothing in isolation; its connections — history, comorbidities, findings — are the diagnosis
meaning emerges by tracing what connects to what: the same fever means different things on different evidence trails
the shared classification everyone maps their local shorthand to, so two hospitals can exchange a diagnosis and mean the same thing
medicine records what it does not yet know as a first-class state — 'query appendicitis' is honest, actionable uncertainty
